title: Hosts
hint: Which themes and scripts each proxy host gets.
intro: Every proxy host in Nginx Proxy Manager gets the same sub_filter rule (with $host). Which themes and scripts a host gets is set here. Hosts without their own row follow Default (*). Changes are live within a minute.
snippetIntro: Paste this rule under Advanced (Custom Nginx Configuration) of every proxy host. It is the same everywhere; you never need to change it.
snippetLabel: sub_filter rule for every proxy host
optionsError: The rule and choices could not be loaded
ownDomainSummary: Apps with a strict CSP (Vaultwarden, Nextcloud…)
ownDomainText: Some apps refuse stylesheets and scripts from another domain. Serve them from the app's own domain instead: add a location ^~ /alg-thema/ to that proxy host that forwards to cssthema, and use this rule instead of the regular one.
ownDomainLabel: sub_filter rule via the own domain
loadError: The hosts could not be loaded
emptyText: Set up the default first, or import your existing NPM config.
defaultMissingText: Hosts without their own row currently get nothing. Set a default (*) for all other hosts.
deleteDefaultText: Hosts without their own row will then get nothing.
dialogDescription: Themes load in this order: a later one overrides an earlier one.
hostnameHint: E.g. proxmox.yourdomain.com, or * for every host without its own row.
stylesHint: Published themes and CSS files; you may also type another name.
scriptsHint: Empty for apps where no script may run (e.g. a password vault).
unknownHint: Not among the published themes and files.
fieldEnabled: On (off: the host gets nothing, not even the default)
errorHostConflict: That hostname already has a binding.
importDescription: Paste the contents of npm-sub_filter-per-dienst.conf: a # hostname line above each sub_filter line.
